text:
maya (devex): Quick repro for a confusing auth edge: quickstart image was talking to the wrong workspace for new users.

lee (sdk): details?

maya (devex): I followed the quickstart exactly, set PROJECT_KEY in my env, started the container, and calls were attributed to an org key that lived in my local keyring.

ana (platform): that sounds like the loader prioritized keyring entries over explicit env vars.

lee (sdk): oh no. the intended order is env vars first -> keyring -> cloud metadata. if keyring is winning something's wrong.

maya (devex): snippet from container helper: `const token = keyring.get('redwood:token') || process.env.PROJECT_KEY || process.env.ORG_KEY` — so keyring is first.

ana (platform): yeah that's backwards. Also the keyring ids are unscoped so an org token can overwrite project tokens.

lee (sdk): plan: flip loader order to prefer env vars, add namespaced key ids `redwood:project:<id>:token`, and add a startup warning when both ORG and PROJECT tokens are present.

maya (devex): can we also update the quickstart Dockerfile to explicitly unset ORG_KEY so images don't bake it in? tiny change but saves a lot of confusion.

lee (sdk): adding a unit test matrix for env combos and a small migration note for devs with existing keyring entries.

ana (platform): infra note: add CI lint to fail builds that reference ORG_KEY in Dockerfile or build args. I'll open an issue.

bot-ci: issue #778 created: scan Dockerfiles for ORG_KEY usage.

maya (devex): thanks. once PR lands I'll update the tutorial text and add a short callout: "If you see unexpected workspace activity, check ORG_KEY in your env/keyring."

lee (sdk): PR posted: https://git.redwood/sdks/patch/flip-loader-213 — flips loader, namespaces keyring, adds tests. CI green.

maya (devex): great, closing after docs + Dockerfile update. :thumbsup:
